passages.note: Five printed lines ending with ॥ ५४ ॥. Lines 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 are detached marks above lines 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10. A thin piece of the frame's inner top rule (x 586-672, y 261-267) is attached to line 1; a component rule leaves it unlabeled.
लज्जावान्को मूर्ख ... ॥ ५४ ॥. Split rules on lines 14 and 15 take precedence over this range.
The bashful are considered as stupid ... by the evil?. The split rule on line 24 takes precedence over this range.
Cf.—(a) “Bad men give themselves ...” (H. S. Brown). The e of 'done' at the end of line 29 is on no line; a component rule labels it note-cf-a.

(b) “दोषान्वेषणमेव ...” (श्रीकविभट्टकृते पद्यसंग्रहे). Its closing quotation mark after दुर्ग्रहः sits high, in the band of the (H. S. Brown). line above, which the line finder put it on; a component rule labels it note-cf-b.

unit_definition: One passage per verse, per translation or gist paragraph, per heading, and per separately set note item below the rule. Joining the note items, or the heading to its paragraph, is a grouping difference, not an ownership error.
non_text: Rules, and large components that are thin and horizontal (the top and bottom of the page frame), are labeled separator by the builder. The vertical frame bars, which the line finder classes as large components, stay unlabeled. Three short frame pieces that the line finder attached to text lines 14, 15 and 24 are left unlabeled by split rules. The 'Digitized by Google' watermark is not in the ink mask. The piece of the inner top rule attached to line 1 is left unlabeled by a component rule.
